description: The GCC-KNC project's card: Xeon Phi x100 with 61 cores at 1.238 GHz and 16 GB GDDR5 (7120-class). Latencies, throughputs and bandwidths below were measured natively on this card by the project's characterization runs (S6-03 on 2026-11-06, S8-01/S8-10/S8-12/S8-17 on 2026-11-07..09), recorded in docs/research/knc-characterization.md of the gcc_knc repository. Units are TSC ticks per operation at one thread unless stated; the TSC (about 1232 MHz) and the core clock (1238 MHz, governor performance) agree within 0.5%, so ticks are treated as core cycles.
native_measurement_ids: S6-03: card_run jobs claude-0380b2ec, claude-7191652b, claude-b1f534af (2026-11-06), .work/_shared/S6-03/knc-char.mic, median of five group medians, spread <2% unless starred

calibration.statement: Core timing is inherited from core-x100-measured (measured or derived on this card: S6-03, S8-01, S8-12, S12-31). Predictions were compared with 119 characterization rows (held-out median error 0.9/0.4/1.6% at 1/2/4 threads, ranking 0.989) and with 105 held-out compiled rows from the binaries that ran on the card (S12-31 row loops, HPCG kernels L2-resident and memory-bound, S12-30 sparse products): median error 3.1%, right winner 39 of 39 pairs more than 5% apart. The decision bar's error and ranking criteria are met; its breadth (loops from at least five M4 programs) is not: shapes outside validated_shapes are unvalidated_scenario_estimate. Recording run of the final engine (profile hash 2058f0ec...).

register_vector_chain_l1.evidence: S6-03 vector .lat/.rt rows, swizzles, conversions, C7, C9 register chains at 1/2/4 threads
register_vector_chain_l1.note: L1-resident vector arithmetic with register dependencies, pairing and loop control; worst case vpaddd.rt at two threads (measured 2.32, a flagged row)

scalar_mask_l1.evidence: S6-03 scalar_add/xor, kmov/kand/kxor rows, pair.* rows, agi.gap0-4
scalar_mask_l1.note: scalar integer and mask chains, pairing, address-generation interlock

x87_register_chain.note: x87 register chains and the divider occupancy; memory-form x87 chains not separately measured

l1_l2_dependent_loads.evidence: S6-03 l1.load_lat/rt, l2.load_lat/rt, memory.load_lat, masked/convert store-reload chains
l1_l2_dependent_loads.note: pointer chases and independent loads with L1/L2-resident or cold footprints; independent store/reload pairs are over-charged (spill_reload.rt +78%)

l1_resident_stores_prefetch_pairing.evidence: S6-03 l1.store_normal, masked_store rows, store_stream rows, C2 prefetch pairing
l1_resident_stores_prefetch_pairing.note: stores to resident lines, no-read stores, vprefetch0/1 pairing

x87_row_loop_l1.evidence: S12-31 microbench, 65 held-out variants (tests/heldout_native/s12-31-microbench), one thread
x87_row_loop_l1.note: x87 sparse row products with data in L1, converted from the binary with code layout; padding, prefixes and loop-body order included

x87_sparse_rows_l2.evidence: S12-31 HPCG toy, 16 held-out kernels (ComputeSPMV_ref, ComputeSYMGS_ref, eight builds), one thread
x87_sparse_rows_l2.note: HPCG-shaped x87 sparse rows with the matrix resident in L2

x87_sparse_rows_memory_stream.evidence: S12-31 HPCG 104-cubed SpMV, 8 held-out builds, one thread
x87_sparse_rows_memory_stream.note: the same shape streaming from memory on one thread (TLB, L2 prefetcher and memory service modeled); not validated at several threads

x87_sparse_rows_l1.evidence: S12-30 small cases, 16 held-out rows, one thread
x87_sparse_rows_l1.note: random-column sparse products into a 32 KiB x: uniformly 12 to 18% slow (L1 conflict misses under true LRU, input instance), rankings right; the error exceeds the 10% bar, so results stay unvalidated_scenario_estimate

card.model.value: Xeon Phi x100, 61 cores, 1.238 GHz, 16 GB (7120-class; exact SKU not recorded)
card.model.source: project config; core count and clock read on the card (S6-01 R1 logs)

card.clock_hz.source: S6-01 run logs (governor performance, 1,238,094 kHz; S8-17 C12 confirmed no throttling)

card.tsc_hz.source: S6-01 R1 lines 245-265 (about 1232.199 MHz); invariance not proven

card.usable_cores.source: S6-01 placement protocol: cores 0-59 for jobs, OS core CPUs {0,241,242,243} excluded

card.memory_bytes.source: Intel 7120 specification; project card-full.json allows 13312 MB per job

card.peak_memory_bandwidth_gbs.source: Intel 7120 specification; R08 ('Peak Memory Bandwidth of Xeon Phi SE10P is 352 GB/s')

card.sustained_bandwidth_gbs.unit: GB/s of useful bytes by traffic type, whole card, best measured configuration
card.sustained_bandwidth_gbs.source: read_only 186.14, read_modify_write 179.39, write_ngo 169.74: S11-06 sweep 2 winner table (lead run 2026-11-12, 2048 MiB x 32 passes, five samples, completion envelope; read with 120 threads, the others with 60; docs/research/knc-memory-bandwidth.md and knc-machine.yaml stream_sweep2_bandwidth). write_normal 82.4: S8-01 C1 60-core table, slowest-worker completion estimate (c1_completed_store_bandwidth)
card.sustained_bandwidth_gbs.uncertainty: Each value is the winner of a configuration sweep (threads, page size, prefetch distance), not a configuration-independent ceiling: the same read loop with 4 KiB pages and 60 threads measured 147.2 GB/s, an fp32 GEMV 125.3 GB/s, and a second read screen 189.1 GB/s. 0.2.x held worker-median figures (156.5 read-modify-write, 226.1 NGO), which the machine file says not to use as completed card throughput. Excludes read-for-ownership traffic.

card.barrier_ns.source: S8-10 C11: fan-in-4 tree 5,521-6,469 ns; one shared counter 26,810-28,410 ns (three launches)

latency.remote_l2_line_ns.unit: ns per load of a line in another core's L2
latency.remote_l2_line_ns.source: S8-10 C11: 190.6-195.0 ns, near and far owner alike
latency.remote_l2_line_ns.uncertainty: R08 reports ~275 ns on SE10P; R22 shows physical address matters.

latency.memory.source: S6-03 memory.load_lat 356.53 per dependent hop at one thread (idle) minus the first-level TLB miss of 29 cycles (tlb.l1_miss_penalty_cycles): the measured chain touches a new 4 KiB page at every hop and the TLB sub-model charges that miss explicitly. 0.2.x used 357 and double-counted it when the TLB was modeled.
latency.memory.uncertainty: assumes every hop of the measured chain missed the first-level TLB; 357.96 at two threads, 365.76 at four

memory.lines_per_cycle_per_core_measured.unit: lines per core cycle, sequential loads at four threads with the hardware prefetcher active
memory.lines_per_cycle_per_core_measured.source: S6-03 memory.load_rt 77.92 per thread at four threads (19.5 ticks per line per core, about 4 GB/s per core at one core)
memory.lines_per_cycle_per_core_measured.note: Informational: includes the L2 hardware prefetcher, which the simulator does not model.

memory.core_service_cycles_per_line.unit: core cycles between memory fills for one core (sequential stream, hardware prefetcher active)
memory.core_service_cycles_per_line.source: S6-03 memory.load_rt per core at four threads 19.48 ticks per line (37.35 at one thread); modeled as the integer 20
memory.core_service_cycles_per_line.uncertainty: measured with the hardware prefetcher streaming; one core alone on the card; not a card-level bandwidth share
